items.title: Work Environment Factors and Work Efficiency Among Filipino US Registered Nurses in Remote Utilization Management Roles in The United States Healthcare System
items.abstract: Remote Utilization Management has emerged as an alternative nursing role for Filipino United States Registered Nurses, yet evidence concerning their working conditions and efficiency remains limited. This study examined the relationship between work environment factors and work efficiency and developed an evidence-based training program. Methods: A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was used among 158 Filipino USRNs working in remote Utilization Management. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring physical work environment, technological support, workload, organizational support, communication, work-life balance, leadership, productivity, accuracy, timeliness, decision making, and job performance. Frequency, percentage, mean, independent samples t test, analysis of variance, Welch’s analysis, and Pearson correlation were employed. Results: Respondents generally reported high levels of work environment and work efficiency. Physical work environment and technological support were the strongest workplace dimensions, while workload and work-life balance were comparatively lowest. Quality and accuracy emerged as the strongest efficiency dimension, whereas productivity was comparatively lowest. Work environment and efficiency differed significantly according to educational attainment, civil status, nursing experience, and remote Utilization Management experience, but not according to age or sex. All work environment dimensions had very strong positive relationships with productivity, accuracy, timeliness, decision making, and overall performance. Discussion: The findings indicate that favorable physical, technological, organizational, relational, and psychosocial conditions are integral to efficient remote nursing practice. The REMOTE-UM EXCEL Program was proposed to strengthen ergonomics, technology competence, workflow management, communication, evidence based decisions, leadership, psychological safety, and work-life boundaries. Organizations should implement integrated workplace interventions and evaluate their effects through longitudinal and performance-based measures to support sustained quality, employee well-being, and organizational effectiveness.

items.title: Workplace Violence, Psychosocial Risks and Mental Health Across Healthcare Professional Groups
items.abstract: Healthcare workers are exposed to workplace violence, yet the extent and nature of this exposure may differ considerably across professional groups. Psychosocial working conditions, including high work demands, emotional demands, working-time pressures and employment relations, may shape the conditions in which workplace violence occurs and is experienced. This study investigates psychosocial risks, workplace violence and symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress among nurses, physicians, healthcare assistants and administrative staff, and examines whether workplace violence is statistically associated with the relationship between psychosocial risks and these symptoms. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 289 Portuguese healthcare workers using three validated instruments: the Psychosocial Risk Factors Scale (INSAT_ERPS), the Aggression and Violence at Work Scale and the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21). Group differences were tested with Kruskal–Wallis tests, associations with Spearman correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses were performed using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. Results showed that workplace violence affected all professional groups but was more intense among nurses. Psychosocial risk was strongly associated with workplace violence, and this association did not differ across professional groups. However, neither psychosocial risks nor violence were associated with depression, anxiety or stress, and no statistically significant indirect association was observed. These findings highlight the importance of addressing workplace violence as an organizational and occupational health issue rather than a problem confined to specific professions.

items.title: YQX+: Benchmarking Probabilistic Modeling of Piano Performance Expression
items.abstract: A written music score specifies what notes should be played, but much of the musical meaning of a performance comes from how those notes are interpreted: pianists shape timing, dynamics, tempo, and articulation to communicate structure, style, and emotion. Modeling this expressive aspect of music matters for music education, digital performance rendering, and creative AI systems, and is difficult precisely because the same score admits many different but musically valid interpretations.In this paper, we present YQX+, a benchmarking framework for probabilistic modeling of expressive piano performance. YQX+ shifts the focus from demonstrating a single rendering system to comparing how different models capture the expressive variation observed in human performance. To make that comparison possible, it fixes the prediction task, a shared multi-scale contextual feature representation, and a common evaluation protocol, so that model families are trained and compared on equal footing. Given a symbolic score, every model in the suite predicts the same note-level expressive parameters, including beat period, velocity, timing deviation, and articulation ratio, from features that capture local note context, harmonic texture, phrase structure, and score markings. The suite takes the original YQX Gaussian mixture model (GMM) as its reference point and extends it to XGBoost, variational autoencoders, and conditional flow-matching models.To support perceptual evaluation, we also introduce PerformanceMOS, a data-driven estimator of perceived expressive quality and performance skill from symbolic piano performances. Experiments show that larger-capacity XGBoost and \((\beta)\)-VAE models achieve lower timing and articulation errors than prior baselines, including DExter and VirtuosoNet, and obtain the highest predicted mean opinion scores (MOS). These findings establish YQX+ as a systematic benchmark for probabilistic modeling of piano performance expression, with PerformanceMOS providing a scalable proxy for human listening evaluation. The code, trained models, and evaluation scripts are available at \texttt{https://github.com/kkwsts/YQX-Plus}.

items.abstract: Computer-based managerial systems are part of the digital infrastructure of work, with potential implications for employee demands and discretion. Drawing on Job Demands-Resources theory, this study examines task allocation, work scheduling and performance monitoring as distinct functions and their parallel indirect associations with engagement and intention to quit through work intensity and autonomy. Weighted least squares mean- and variance-adjusted structural equation models were estimated for 26,504 employees in 35 European countries using the 2024 European Working Conditions Survey. The measures capture reported computer involvement rather than verified artificial intelligence capabilities. Engagement and autonomy were modelled as latent factors, and quit intention as an ordinal outcome. All three practices were positively associated with work intensity. Task allocation was positively associated with autonomy, whereas monitoring was negatively associated with autonomy; scheduling’s negative autonomy association was less robust to contextual fixed effects. Task allocation showed opposing indirect engagement associations through intensity and autonomy, whereas monitoring showed negative associations through both pathways. Intensity-related indirect associations with quit intention were consistently positive, while autonomy-related indirect associations were not statistically significant in the primary or fixed-effects models. Sensitivity analyses supported the main directional patterns, while exploratory country diagnostics indicated incomplete measurement invariance and heterogeneous slopes. The findings inform the evaluation of digital management by distinguishing functions associated with greater demands and greater autonomy from those associated with greater demands and reduced autonomy. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal mediation or uniform cross-country relationships.

items.title: Consider the Dashboard: Exploring a visual medium of datafication
items.abstract: Dashboards are central to contemporary organizations aiming to ‘datafy’ decision making and management practices. As one of the primary media through which people engage with digital data in organizational contexts, dashboards shape how data is accessed and perceived. Despite their ubiquity, there is limited understanding of how dashboards mediate data visibility and influence observers’ perceptions of the data. Drawing on theories of mediation and diagrammatics, this paper analyzes the ‘generic form’ shared by all dashboards. It then identifies the modes of observation encouraged by dashboards, revealing how they position their observers. While grounded in theoretical arguments, the analysis incorporates empirical examples from a study on the datafication of Human Resource Management. The paper makes two key contributions. It emphasizes the critical role of visual forms in datafication processes, and it highlights the organizational implications of the use of a specific kind of visual medium: the dashboard.

items.title: Counting crashes is not enough: developing an exposure-based high risk network for e-scooter safety
items.abstract: Shared e-scooters are now common in urban transportation, but safety planning remains limited by a lack of exposure-based, spatially detailed crash risk measures. This study applied an exposure-based approach to identify high-risk e-scooter corridors in Nashville, Tennessee, combining 92 police-reported, motor-vehicle-involved e-scooter crashes with trip-kilometer exposure data over a 45-month period. Crashes were assigned to corridors by rider direction of travel, and rates were calculated per 100,000 vehicle kilometers traveled (VKT) citywide and by corridor. Across more than five million e-scooter kilometers of exposure, the citywide crash rate was 1.84 per 100,000 VKT, and 82.6% of crashes occurred at intersections or driveways. The 25 corridors accounted for 75.0% of crashes and 70.9% of VKT, with a combined rate (1.94 per 100,000 VKT) statistically indistinguishable from the rest of Nashville (1.58; p = 0.34). Corridor-level rates were nonetheless heterogeneous (chi-square = 96.17, df = 24, p < 0.001), with unadjusted rates ranging from 0.69 to 24.49 crashes per 100,000 VKT; empirical Bayes shrinkage reduced this spread to roughly 3.7-fold. Three corridors, Shelby Avenue, 21st Avenue, and West End Avenue, exceeded the citywide rate individually, with the first two remaining significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Exposure-adjusted corridor rates gave a different picture of risk than crash counts alone: citywide averages concealed substantial street-level variation, supporting corridor-level exposure measures as a screening tool for micromobility safety, though individual designations remain exploratory rather than confirmatory. These results let agencies combine trip and crash data to target safety investment at high-risk corridors.

items.title: Elite Strength and Conditioning Coaches as First-Line Users of Sports-Science Technology: Dashboard Workarounds in Time-Constrained Decision-Making
items.abstract: Elite strength and conditioning (S&C) coaches occupy a critical but underexamined position as first-line users of sports-science technology, responsible for translating raw athlete-monitoring data into immediate training decisions. Through seven semi-structured interviews with elite S & C coaches across NCAA Division I, professional, and Olympic contexts, we identify four recurring breakdowns in their daily data work: fragmented vendor ecosystems, metric overload, scale and staffing constraints and staff turnover. Static mockup elicitation during interviews revealed a consistent preference for simple, interpretable interfaces that foreground selected metrics and concise explanations over dense data displays. We position elite S&C coaches as a distinct user group whose needs are poorly served by current systems, and propose four design priorities: integration stability, selective metrics with contextual explanation, scale-aware views, and governance continuity, to guide future coach-facing sports-science interface design.

items.title: Empirical Analysis of Driver Behavior at Uncontrolled Midblock Crosswalks: Influence of Bike Lane Buffer Types
items.abstract: At unsignalized midblock crosswalks (UMCs), visual obstructions created by bike lane buffers can substantially affect drivers’ pedestrian detection and yielding behavior. However, limited evidence is available regarding how different types of bike lane buffers influence driving performance through changes in visual attention and cognitive workload. To address this issue, four representative bike lane buffer scenarios—Lawn, Railing, Bush, and Tree—were developed in a driving simulation environment. Vehicle operation parameters and eye-tracking data were collected simultaneously to investigate drivers’ behavioral and visual responses while approaching a crosswalk. The results showed that highly obstructive buffers significantly delayed pedestrian detection and weakened drivers’ early risk perception. In the Bush and Tree scenarios, pedestrians were detected at distances of only about 18 m from the crosswalk, representing a reduction of more than 40% compared with the low-obstruction conditions. As a consequence, drivers exhibited lower terminal braking speeds, higher maximum deceleration rates, and more abrupt braking maneuvers. The mean braking initiation distance in the Bush and Tree scenarios was approximately 48 m, which was more than 10 m shorter than that observed under the Lawn and Railing conditions. Eye-tracking analyses further revealed that highly obstructive environments significantly increased fixation duration on roadside areas while reducing the effective visual search range. In addition, the proportions of saccades and blinks decreased to approximately 3%, whereas the coefficient of variation of pupil diameter increased to 0.23, indicating elevated cognitive workload and mental stress. These findings demonstrate that visual obstructions associated with bike lane buffers can adversely affect drivers’ hazard perception, visual search behavior, and braking responses. The study provides empirical evidence to support the safety evaluation and design optimization of bike lane buffers near unsignalized midblock crosswalks.

items.title: GoldMind: a teacher-centred knowledge management system for higher education – lessons from iterative design
items.abstract: Designing Knowledge Management Systems (KMSs) for higher education requires addressing complex human–technology interactions, especially where staff turnover and changing roles create challenges for reusing knowledge. While advances in process mining and Generative AI enable new ways of designing features to support knowledge management, existing KMSs often overlook the realities of educators' workflows, leading to low adoption and limited impact. This paper presents findings from a two-year human-centred design study with 108 higher education teachers, examining iterative co-design and evaluation of GoldMind – a KMS supporting in-the-flow knowledge management during digital teaching tasks. Through three design–evaluation cycles, we examined teachers' task-evaluations and how feedback informed refinements. Insights are synthesised across three themes: (1) Technology Lessons from user interaction data, (2) Design Considerations shaped by co-design and usability testing, and (3) Human Factors, including cognitive load and knowledge behaviours, analysed using Epistemic Network Analysis (in the last iteration). This study demonstrates that embedding human-centred, workflow-integrated KMSs can improve task efficiency, reduce cognitive load, and support knowledge reuse, while shaping educators' knowledge management behaviours through context-aware and proactive support. However, findings are based on a single-institution, controlled evaluation, limiting generalisability and requiring longitudinal, in-the-wild studies to assess adoption and impact.

items.title: LLM-Generated Design Problems for Assessing Higher-Order Thinking in Project-Based Learning
items.abstract: Project-based learning (PjBL) is common in computing education, but traditional assessments of PjBL often fail to capture higher-order thinking (HOT), especially in transfer contexts. This study introduces ''design problems'' (DPs): concise, scenario-based prompts that require applying project concepts in new situations, to address this gap. We examined instructor perceptions, the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate DPs, and student experiences. Surveys of 31 instructors, evaluation of 80 LLM-generated DPs, and student performance data showed that while instructors value DPs, creation effort is a barrier. LLMs helped by producing high-quality prompts with strong expert agreement. Students rated DPs from different LLMs similarly, and their performance on DP tasks showed negligible correlation with traditional project grades, suggesting DPs may capture distinct aspects of HOT. Keystroke data also suggested deeper cognitive engagement of students through planning and revision behaviors. Overall, DPs appear to be a useful complement to traditional assessments, especially in situations where AI use or collaboration may undermine individual learning.

items.title: Occupational Exposure to N,N-Dimethylformamide and Hepatotoxicity among Synthetic Leather Workers in Bangladesh: Implications for Workplace Health and Labour Law Compliance
items.abstract: Purpose : N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) is a polar aprotic solvent that is extensively used in the production of synthetic leather, polyurethane products, resins, adhesives and surface coatings. Potential sources of occupational exposures are mixing, formulation, coating, solvent transfer, cleaning, maintenance, and spill-response. DMF may be inhaled and absorbed through intact skin, which means that total internal dose for a particular worker may be underestimated by only measuring DMF in the air. Liver is a known target organ of DMF toxicity, and reports of increased liver enzymes and, less frequently, clinically significant liver injury have been reported in workers occupationally exposed to DMF. Increases in liver-function tests, however, are non-specific and can occur in people who drink too much alcohol and/or are obese, and/or may be caused by metabolic disease associated with steatotic liver disease, viral hepatitis, certain medicines (prescribed or not) or other exposures that may occur at work. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation of possible liver damage from DMF should include exposure history, workplace monitoring, biological monitoring, repeated clinical evaluations, and the careful consideration of other causes of liver damage. Objective : The aim of this study is to find the relationship between DMF exposure and liver injury in the workers working in the synthetic leather, polyurethane, resin and surface-coating industries. It will consider exposure by inhalation and skin contact, estimate internal exposure as measured by urinary markers, review liver-function patterns as they change over time, determine if another source of liver injury or exposure may have occurred, and determine if a failure of workplace controls or medical surveillance could have led to exposure. The results will help to inform evidence-based occupational-health and medico-legal decisions about the possibility and level of occupational contribution to liver disease. Methods : An occupational-health study using a mixed-methods approach will be conducted with workers who may be at risk for DMF, such as mixers, formulators, coating operators, solvent-transfer workers, cleaners, maintenance workers, and waste-handling workers. A standardised occupational history will document job titles, length of employment, work patterns, frequency of tasks, use of DMF containing products, past chemical exposures, spillages, symptoms, hygiene practices and use and suitability of personal protective equipment (PPE). Task specific workplace exposure assessments will be carried out and personal air sampling will be used, wherever possible, especially during transfer, mixing, coating, cleaning and maintenance activities. The results of the air-monitoring will be evaluated against relevant occupational exposure concentrations with an understanding that an exposure below the airborne concentration limit does not mean there is no significant dermal absorption. The dermal exposure potential will be evaluated by conducting facility observations and interviews with workers, which will include direct hands-on contact with the material, use of contaminated gloves and clothing, gloves used, gloves replaced, local exhaust ventilation, housekeeping, spill control, washing facility, training, and working practices. The urinary concentrations of N-methylformamide (NMF) and N-acetyl-S-(N-methylcarbamoyl)cysteine (AMCC) will be measured for internal DMF exposure. These are markers of systemic exposure from all routes of exposure including inhalation and skin contact. Ideally, urine samples will be collected at the end of shift and end of work week, or at other suitable times depending on the toxicokinetic properties of the biomarker. Urine dilutions, e.g. creatinine, specific gravity etc., will be corrected and results interpreted taking into account the timing of the sample, the analytical procedure and available biological guidance values. Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels, bilirubin, albumin and international normalised ratio (INR) will be measured at regular intervals. These tests will assist in the identification of hepatocellular, cholestatic or mixed liver injury patterns and be useful in identifying transient, persistent or progressive liver injuries. Symptoms such as fatigue, nausea, abdominal discomfort, jaundice, pruritus and constitutional symptoms will also be recorded. Systematic assessment of potential confounding factors and alternative diagnosis. Alcohol intake, BMI, presence of diabetes, metabolic disease, pre-existing liver disease, other hepatotoxic chemicals and drug or supplement use will be recorded. Investigations may consist of a hepatology specialist review, abdominal ultrasound and hepatitis B and C testing, where clinically appropriate and consented to. There will be a structured medico-legal review, combining evidence from 4 domains – exposure, biological plausibility, individual clinical disease and duty of care. Occupational history and occupational monitoring will support the results of urinary biomarkers as evidence of internal exposure. The adequacy of engineering controls, local exhaust ventilation, training, spill management, hazard communication and medical surveillance will be taken into account in the duty of care assessment. Challenging with the drug after a possible hepatotoxic reaction will not take place. Expected Results : The study will not pre-judge causation as there is currently no data. It is anticipated to see if the workers with high overall or task specific exposure would have higher levels of urinary NMF and AMCC, and if these workers would have more frequent and persistent liver-test abnormalities. It will also be evaluated if liver enzymes improve if DMF exposure is reduced or eliminated, if follow up is available. Importantly, the analysis will differentiate isolated elevations of enzymes from a pattern of occupationally related disease. Conclusions :Concurring inhalational and dermal exposure to DMF is an occupational-health hazard that can be prevented. Task-based exposure assessment, urinary biomarkers, serial liver tests, clinical differential diagnosis and structured medico-legal analysis is a better approach for assessing possible occupational hepatotoxicity than liver enzymes alone. Decisions regarding the possibility, probability and highly probable occupational contribution will be based on the overall evidence and distinct from legal liability.PPE, training, spillage or medical surveillance had a significant impact on the workers.

items.title: Organizational responses to near-miss reporting and perceived organizational support among Japanese workers: a longitudinal cohort study
items.abstract: Near-miss events in the workplace serve as important signals for occupational accident prevention, and organizational responses to near-miss reports may influence employees’ perceived organizational support (POS). the association between organizational response patterns to near-miss reports and POS has not been sufficiently examined. This longitudinal study used data from an online cohort study of Japanese workers conducted at baseline (March 2023) and follow-up (December 2023). The analysis included 1,168 non-managerial workers who had experienced at least one near-miss event. Participants were categorized into four groups based on reporting behavior and the adequacy of organizational responses: reporting with adequate response, reporting with partial response, reporting with no response (reference), and no reporting. Associations between response patterns and POS at follow-up were examined using linear regression analysis. Employees in the reporting with adequate response (B = 2.16, 95% CI: 0.71–3.61) and reporting with partial response (B = 1.68, 95% CI: 0.12–3.23) groups showed significantly higher POS at follow-up compared with the reporting with no response group. The no reporting group also showed significantly higher POS (B = 1.63, 95% CI: 0.13–3.12). No significant moderating effect of company size was observed. These findings suggest that the quality of organizational responses to near-miss reports is associated with POS regardless of company size. Employees who reported near-miss events but received no organizational response showed the lowest POS, even lower than those who did not report. These findings highlight the importance of adequate follow-up and communication after near-miss reporting.

items.title: Patience and Organization Studies: Festina lente
items.abstract: Modern organizations often valorize speed and immediacy, treating acceleration as the dominant temporal logic of organizational life. Challenging this logic remains difficult, however, because organization studies lacks a well-developed conceptual language for alternative ways of engaging with time. We propose patience as one such alternative. Building on recent work on Eigenzeit, we argue that organizations can partially uncouple from external temporal pressures and develop forms of relative temporal autonomy that enable the orchestration of differentiated temporalities. While Eigenzeit highlights how organizations establish and sustain a temporality of their own amid complex temporal demands, less attention has been paid to the pacing through which this temporality is enacted in everyday organizational life. We therefore foreground pacing as the practical means by which organizations enact and sustain their own temporality. Within this context, patience emerges as a particular mode of pacing grounded in purposeful deceleration. To make this mode of pacing analytically visible, we identify four manifestations of organizational patience: waiting, restraining, forbearing, and persisting. Drawing on insights from the sociology of time, organization studies, and philosophy, we show how these manifestations represent distinct ways of pacing organizational activities by holding time open, delaying intervention, staying with difficulty, and sustaining engagement over time. By reframing patience as a distinctive mode of pacing rather than passive inactivity, we show how organizations cultivate and sustain an Eigenzeit through practices that contribute to the orchestration of competing temporal demands. This perspective advances organization studies by illuminating how temporal orchestration is accomplished through everyday organizational interactions and how patience enables organizations to sustain resilience and meaningful engagement in the face of acceleration pressures.

items.title: Physiological Correlates of Passenger-Facing HMI Communication in Automated Driving
items.abstract: Passenger-facing vehicle interfaces must inform without disrupting non-driving activities. This study related HMI communication during fully automated driving to passenger physiology and interaction quality during concurrent reading. Twenty-six participants completed a no-communication Baseline drive and one HMI drive with abstract auditory-tactile cues (Simple) or synthesised speech (Extended); 24 contributed physiological data. Electrodermal activity (EDA) was the primary measure, with User Experience Questionnaire ratings. Because HMI variant was assigned between participants, participant-level analyses provided primary condition inference. Mean EDA was lower in both HMI conditions than Baseline, but no contrast was statistically supported (Simple–Baseline −73.1, 95% CI [−160.3, 14.0], p = 0.092; Extended–Baseline −44.7, p = 0.296; Extended–Simple 28.4, p = 0.614). No UEQ scale survived multiplicity correction. Segment-level mixed-effects models (803 segments) reproduced this ordering with narrower intervals reflecting repeated observations, not independent assignments. Participant-level contrasts matched the unit of assignment; segment-level models characterised temporal physiological variation.

items.title: Posture in practice: heightened awareness of surgical resident ergonomics
items.abstract: Background Ergonomics is an often-overlooked component of operative education. Early intervention can protect residents from physical stress and long-term musculoskeletal injury. Our aim is to evaluate residents during a simulated suturing exercise and assess the impact of self-evaluation on ergonomics. Methods Following informed consent, surgical residents performed a simulated complex wound closure, blinded to the study’s focus. Following initial closure, residents reviewed their videos with an ergonomic self-assessment guide, repeated the exercise, and completed a post-survey. Representative video clips were analyzed to measure elbow, spine, and neck angles. Standard angles were defined as 90–110° for elbow, < 10° for spine, and < 25° for neck. Results Twenty residents participated across four post-graduate years (PGY): five PGY-4, four PGY-3, four PGY-2, and seven PGY-1. Across all participants, we found significant reduction in spine (12.5° vs 5.1°, p = 0.016) and neck (58.5° vs 46.4°, p = 0.004) angle during the second exercise, but no difference in elbow angle (102.7° vs 101.7°, p = 0.744). The post-survey revealed most residents think about their ergonomics in the operating room at least weekly (75%) and feel physical strain (95%). All residents (100%) reported improved awareness of ergonomics and perceived transferability to the clinical setting. Discussion Our study demonstrated a resident self-assessment of ergonomics led to significant improvement in spinal and neck angles in a simulated exercise with increased awareness of operative ergonomics and perceived transferability to the clinical setting. These findings support integration of ergonomic education early in surgical training to help reduce physical strain and promote operative longevity.

items.title: Street Fights and Court Battles: Incumbent mobilization and the timing of regulatory bans against platform entrants
items.abstract: In this paper, we examine how incumbent-led mobilization against Uber’s platform entry in Europe relates to regulatory bans, public attention, and consumer-side uptake. Combining hand-coded data on taxi-sector tactics and frames with first regulatory bans, Uber app downloads, and Google search interest across 22 European countries from 2012 to 2020, we identify a differentiated temporal pattern. Private tactics are strongly associated with first-ban hazard in the short window following mobilization, whereas lawsuits are positively associated over a longer window. The frames incumbents deploy also matter: legitimacy-challenge frames portraying UberPop as incompatible with lawful and fair competition are more consistently associated with bans than compliance-dispute frames focused on tax or labor obligations. At the same time, private tactics and lawsuits coincide with immediate increases in app downloads and Google search interest, indicating an attention spillover from incumbent contestation. Lawsuit-related download elevations display marginally greater persistence than those associated with private tactics, although this difference is not stronger early after entry. Taken together, the findings show that incumbent mobilization in platform markets can be associated with regulatory bans and consumer-side uptake of the entrants they seek to exclude at the same time. The results establish temporal association, although the direction of influence within this process cannot be isolated.

items.title: The AGI power dilemma and the illusion of safety with humans in the loop
items.abstract: Avoiding loss-of-control events will be key to industry and society as AI technology is employed in various critical processes. In this article, we assess a hypothetical instability situation of an AGI − a singularity event − from a safety science standpoint. We present one way to describe the process of how a real time Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) in its interaction with the environment may set it in a runaway condition. Our goal is clarifying general and structural control issues of strong real time AI for design, safeguarding and legislation. In cybernetics, instability and hence, the risk of loss-of-control, is a core trait of all highly adaptive systems. Such adaptive behavior can manifest as radical reframing – a pivotal process of a system that enables it to solve very hard challenges, and which requires it to redefine its core concepts, goals, values, plans and procedures. What emerges is the AGI power dilemma ; a double-bind between performance and controllability of a real time system. We discuss the consequences for human control of AGI and prospects for safeguarding when optimizing for power and speed. Moreover, we conclude that the human in the loop approach gives an illusion of safety when the AI is optimized for power.

items.title: What You See Is (Not) What You Got: The Human Factor in PDF Signature Verification
items.abstract: Signed PDF documents have legally binding value under frameworks such as the EU's eIDAS regulation. In this work, we present Genuine PDF Forgeries, a novel attack class that focuses on human factors in signature validation. Our attacks target the disconnect between cryptographically verifiable signer certificates and human-visible signature blocks embedded in documents. We analyze our attacks against 23 PDF viewers and validation tools across desktop platforms and the web. We find that nine of the 13 viewers that automatically report signature validity hide authenticated signer information behind additional user interaction. We then evaluate the attack in twin deception-based online studies with 584 EU-based participants. To further validate the impact, we perform a highly tailored real-world attack study with six trials within two privacy-sensitive organizations. Five of six organizational trials accepted requests authenticated using the forged visual identity. In the online studies (total n=584), the most effective attack variant deceives 71.9% of eligible participants on first impression, and 57.3% continue to be deceived even after we prompt for additional introspection. We derive viewer-side countermeasures and prototype a safeguard that overlays the untrusted signature block with signer information obtained from the validated certificate. Our results show that boolean validity indicators, not associated with the authenticated signer identity, are insufficient in practice.
